bib.title: Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning in Large Language Models with One Training Example

read.skipped: Plot axis-tick debris of Figures 7-15 (about 600 lines of numbers) was skimmed, not read; all prose, tables and appendices read.

question: To what extent can the RLVR training dataset be reduced while keeping performance comparable to the full dataset?
hypothesis: Base models already hold strong reasoning ability, so a single well-chosen example with verifiable reward should be enough to elicit it.
contributions: One example (pi_1 or pi_13) used as the whole RLVR training set matches the 1.2k DSR-sub subset on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B (MATH500 36.0 to 73.6; 6-benchmark average 17.6 to 35.7).
1(few)-shot RLVR works across models (Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B/7B, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B) and algorithms (GRPO, PPO).
Post-saturation generalization: test accuracy keeps rising after training accuracy on the single example saturates.
Cross-category generalization and more frequent self-reflection words under 1-shot RLVR.
Ablations: policy gradient loss is the main driver (not weight decay, so not grokking); entropy loss with a suitable coefficient helps; entropy loss alone gives a gain.
Discussion of format correction, label robustness and prompt modification.

method.summary: GRPO with a binary outcome reward (verl pipeline) is run on a training set of 1, 2, 4, 16 or 1209 math problems, where single examples are ranked by the variance of their per-epoch training accuracy (historical variance score) from a 500-step run on the full pool. The single example is duplicated to fill the 128 batch. Checkpoints are evaluated on six math benchmarks plus ARC.
method.task: RL with verifiable reward for mathematical reasoning

datasets.name: DSR-sub (random subset of DeepScaleR-Preview-Dataset)
datasets.split: random subset; also instance pool for choosing pi_j
datasets.source: DeepScaleR-Preview-Dataset (Luo et al. 2025), AIME 1984-2023, AMC pre-2023, Omni-MATH, Still
datasets.preprocessing: ranked by historical variance score from 500 steps of Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B training; ranking kept fixed for all experiments

datasets.name: MATH500
datasets.source: OpenAI (Lightman et al. 2023), subset of MATH test (5,000)

other.use: checks whether the response contains the correct answer regardless of \boxed{}

training.objective: GRPO loss = policy gradient (clipped, group-normalized advantage) + beta*KL + alpha*entropy; binary 0-1 outcome reward; no format reward (format reward used only as a baseline)
training.lr: 1e-6 (stated in the DeepSeek-R1-Distill paragraph of B.4; inferred: default for all runs, not stated separately)
training.batch_size: 128 train batch and 128 mini-batch; 8 responses per prompt, so 8 gradient updates per rollout step; single example duplicated to 128
training.seq_len: max prompt 1024, max response 3072 (8192 for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B)
training.precision: verl creates the model in fp32 (checkpoints saved fp32); original models are bf16
training.regularisation: KL coefficient beta = 0.001; entropy loss coefficient alpha = -0.001 (also -0.003 in one ablation)
training.hardware: 8 A100 GPUs per training experiment; 4 GPUs for evaluation

other.data_selection: historical variance score v_i = var(s_i,1..s_i,E), E epochs of per-example training accuracy; 500-step run on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B

inference.decoding: temperature 0 for MATH500, Minerva Math, OlympiadBench; temperature 0.6 for AIME24, AIME25, AMC23
inference.samples: AIME24, AIME25, AMC23: test set repeated 8 times, avg@8; DeepSeek-R1-Distill: avg@16 for MATH500/Minerva/OlympiadBench and avg@64 for AIME24/AIME25/AMC23; evaluation seed 0
inference.prompting: qwen25-math-cot template for Qwen models; original chat templates for Llama and distilled models; training prompts end with 'Let's think step by step and output the final answer within \boxed{}.'

other.checkpoint_selection: best average over 6 benchmarks by default; best per-benchmark in Tables 3, 5, 9, 11 (MATH500 and AIME24 only)

metrics.name: avg@k / pass@1
metrics.definition: mean accuracy over k samples per question, with Qwen2.5-Math evaluation pipeline

metrics.name: Pass@8
metrics.definition: fraction of questions solved in at least one of 8 samples

metrics.name: Average over 6 benchmarks
metrics.definition: mean of MATH500, AIME24, AMC23, Minerva Math, OlympiadBench, AIME25

baselines: In-context learning with pi_1 or Qwen official examples
eval.protocol: Single training run per configuration as far as stated; no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported.

prompts.text: The pressure \\( P \\) exerted by wind on a sail varies jointly as the area \\( A \\) of the sail and the cube of the wind’s velocity \\( V \\). When the velocity is \\( 8 \\) miles per hour, the pressure on a sail of \\( 2 \\) square feet is \\( 4 \\) pounds. Find the wind velocity when the pressure on \\( 4 \\) square feet of sail is \\( 32 \\) pounds. Let’s think step by step and output the final answer within \\boxed{}.

limits: Authors concede they did not test larger models such as Qwen2.5-32B (compute) or domains other than math, such as coding.
1-shot RLVR does not save RL compute and may need more: the paper presents a phenomenon, not a method (D.1).
pi_1 was chosen with Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and is not necessarily best for other models; 16-shot often beats 1-shot on other models (D.1). Variance-score selection is not claimed to be optimal.
A large share of the gain is format correction (format reward alone gives 65.0 MATH500 against 73.6); Qwen2.5-Math has about 40% repetition at the end of MATH500 responses.
Explanations (implicit regularization by policy loss, Double Descent link, why entropy loss alone helps) are conjectures; no rigorous analysis.
Single runs, no seeds or error bars reported; best-checkpoint selection on the test benchmarks (reported as best average or best per benchmark) inflates numbers.
Initial-model numbers differ between the downloaded bf16 model and the fp32 verl checkpoint (36.0 vs 39.6 MATH500, Table 7).
Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct is unstable and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B shows a bigger gap between few-shot and full-set RLVR (Table 4, Table 12).
